title: Windows Event Log Capacity and Retention Risk
exclusions: Evaluates explicitly governed local Windows Event Log channels from complete `Get-WinEvent -ListLog` snapshots. For `Retain` mode it detects a full flag or sustained file use above policy; for `Circular` mode it detects a near-capacity channel whose oldest retained event is newer than the required history objective. It does not treat a circular EVTX file being near its configured maximum as failure by itself—circular logs normally overwrite oldest records when full. It does not calculate Splunk index retention, guarantee forwarder checkpoints/backfill, verify every event reached Splunk, protect archived EVTX files, size disk capacity for AutoBackup, detect deliberate log clear, or attest audit/compliance sufficiency. `wevtutil gl` supplies configuration but not current file size, so it is not the utilization authority. Security Event 1104 means the Security log became full under retain/manual-clear behavior; 1105 means automatic backup created a new file; 1108 is an event-processing error. Event 1101 and System 6005 are not overflow substitutes. The example 90% threshold, three five-minute samples, 24/72-hour history objectives, and ten-minute collection allowance are local policies, not Microsoft or Splunk defaults. Missing channels, null/zero maxima, inaccessible oldest records, duplicate snapshots, clock error, and partial manifests are source-health findings. This rule never clears a log, changes LogMode/MaximumSizeInBytes, enables AutoBackup, deletes archives, or modifies audit policy.
evidence: After deployment, retain the signed `TA_windows_eventlog_capacity` collector, policy, and code hash; approved host/channel inventory with history objective and owner; exact collection identity; effective PowerShell input, parsing, routing, and RBAC; complete manifests and channel rows for all three alert samples; same-time `Get-WinEvent -ListLog <channel> | Format-List *`, oldest/newest event, and `wevtutil gl <channel> /f:xml` output; relevant Security 1104/1105/1108 raw XML; free-space/archive evidence for AutoBackup channels; the `windows_eventlog_capacity_retention_risk` saved search, ACL, schedule, dispatch and result history; source-health results; dashboard/alert revisions; policy and exception history; incident disposition; and dated positive, negative, exact-boundary, mode, empty-log, inaccessible, manifest, duplicate, persistence, recovery, and version tests. Preserve byte values, percentage, mode/full flag, record count, oldest/newest/sample epochs, retained hours, required hours, threshold, snapshot IDs, and indexing time. Documentation review created none of these runtime artifacts.

controlTest.positiveScenario: With dispatch fixed at 2026-07-28T12:12:00Z, emit three complete five-minute snapshots at epochs 1785239400, 1785239700, and 1785240000 for one governed channel on `evt-lab-01`. Each manifest expects one channel. Variant A uses `log_name=Security`, `log_mode=retain`, `file_size_bytes=95000000`, `maximum_size_bytes=100000000`, `is_log_full=0`, threshold 90%, and valid oldest/newest times; expect one `retain_capacity` row because 95% is above policy in all samples. Variant B uses `log_mode=circular`, the same 95%, `oldest_record_epoch` only 10 hours before each sample, and `required_history_hours=24`; expect one `circular_retention_shortfall` row. Variant C sets `is_log_full=1` in Retain mode at 80% and must still alert.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero primary rows for each isolated variant: Retain at exactly 90% and not full; Circular at 95% with exactly 24 retained hours; Circular below/equal 90% even with short observed history; AutoBackup at 99%; empty Circular log with `record_count=0` and `history_ready=0`; only two risky samples; risk/healthy/risk; nonconsecutive five-minute epochs; latest expected sample absent; disabled policy; negative/fractional sizes or record count; max zero; file size above 110% of max; invalid mode/full boolean; oldest after newest; wrong source/type/schema; missing/duplicate/incomplete manifest; expected count mismatch; duplicate channel; or two snapshot IDs for one host/slot. Every rejected or unevaluable case must surface in source health. Recovery requires three complete mode-appropriate healthy samples; a bounded exact host/channel exception suppresses delivery only after base-result storage.

dataSources: A deployment-owned read-only PowerShell collector queries an approved channel list every five minutes with Microsoft `Get-WinEvent -ListLog <name>` and bounded `Get-WinEvent -LogName <name> -Oldest|-MaxEvents 1` calls. It emits one complete manifest plus one JSON channel row to deployment-local `index=windows`, `source=windows_eventlog_capacity`, `sourcetype=ms:windows:eventlog:capacity`. Required extracted fields include `host, log_name, is_enabled, log_mode, file_size_bytes, maximum_size_bytes, is_log_full, record_count, oldest_record_epoch, newest_record_epoch, history_ready, sample_epoch, snapshot_id, snapshot_complete, expected_channel_count, capacity_threshold_pct, required_history_hours, alert_enabled, policy_id`. `wevtutil gl /f:xml` corroborates retention/autoBackup/maxSize configuration. Optional Security XML Event IDs 1104, 1105, and 1108 collected by Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) corroborate full/archive/processing events but do not replace the capacity snapshot.
app: A controlled app such as `TA_windows_eventlog_capacity` owns the local PowerShell collector, channel inventory, complete-snapshot/source-health logic, saved search, dashboard, tests, and lookup windows_eventlog_capacity_exceptions.csv. Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) is optional for Security 1104/1105/1108 and adjacent Windows telemetry; it does not provide the custom FileSize/history policy snapshot.

description: Detects sustained Windows Event Log capacity risk at host/channel grain. A Retain channel qualifies when full or strictly above its byte-use threshold; a Circular channel qualifies only when also retaining less history than policy. Three complete consecutive five-minute snapshots, exact channel cardinality, byte units, mode, chronology, policy stability, and freshness are required.
value: Undersized Retain channels can stop accepting events, while undersized Circular channels can overwrite evidence sooner than operations or incident response require. Separating mode-specific behavior turns file size into a defensible retention signal, gives owners time to change capacity or collection architecture, and prevents permanently alerting on healthy circular files that naturally stay near maximum size.
implementation: Deploy a signed read-only collector that queries a governed channel list with `Get-WinEvent -ListLog` plus oldest/newest records every five minutes and emits one atomic manifest. Save the SPL as `windows_eventlog_capacity_retention_risk`, run it two minutes after each slot, and require three risky samples. Use >90% only as a starting Retain threshold; for Circular channels require an approved minimum-history objective as well. Monitor missing/inaccessible snapshots and AutoBackup archive/disk health separately, and corroborate Security full/archive conditions with 1104/1105.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — Event Log Capacity and Retention`: put expected-host/channel collection health and rejected snapshots first. Separate Retain channels that are full/near maximum, Circular channels below history objective, AutoBackup channels/archive health, and disabled governed channels. Show current/max bytes and percentage, LogMode, record count, oldest/newest UTC times, retained versus required hours, three-sample trend, owner, policy, and exception. Provide 24-hour/30-day utilization and retained-history plots plus heat maps by channel/host. Drill down to raw snapshots, `Get-WinEvent -ListLog`, oldest/newest event, Event Viewer channel Properties, `wevtutil gl /f:xml`, Security 1104/1105/1108, disk/archive inventory, forwarder checkpoints/lag, GPO, and recent configuration changes. Unknown or rejected data must not render green.
schema: Custom complete Windows EventLogConfiguration and oldest/newest record snapshot
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM dataset represents EventLogConfiguration FileSize, MaximumSizeInBytes, LogMode, IsLogFull, exact governed-channel inventory, and oldest retained record as one atomic sample. A Change event can show a configuration action but cannot calculate capacity or history coverage. Therefore no `cimSpl` is supplied. Summary acceleration is allowed only if it preserves complete manifests, byte values, mode/full status, oldest/newest chronology, policy, rejected snapshots, and raw parity.

knownFalsePositives:
The detector reports an actual sustained policy breach in valid snapshots. The underlying condition can still be planned, temporary, or governed incorrectly.

1. **Approved audit-policy expansion or incident logging surge** — Microsoft Advanced Audit Policy, Sysmon, PowerShell, Defender, firewall, or application diagnostic changes can sharply increase channel volume. Match GPO/content revision, change ticket, provider/EventID distribution, bytes/events per minute, expected duration, forwarding health, and new retention calculation. Resize from measured churn rather than suppressing the channel indefinitely.

2. **Planned penetration test or incident-response collection** — A purple-team exercise, forensic capture, verbose PowerShell, or temporary provider enablement can shorten circular history. Confirm engagement/case ID, exact hosts/channels, enabled providers, UTC bounds, evidence export, storage plan, and rollback. Preserve the capacity finding as exercise evidence; use a finite notification exception only if retention loss is accepted.

3. **New domain controller, server role, or application onboarding** — Initial synchronization, policy application, software installation, or workload warm-up can create an atypical first-day event rate. Compare build/deployment record, channel configuration baseline, provider mix, forwarder lag, and expected steady state. Recalculate after stabilization; do not assume a 48-hour blind baseline is healthy.

4. **Windows Update, Defender update/scan, or servicing burst** — Servicing can expand Setup, System, Application, Defender, and operational channels. Correlate KB/update ID, servicing/Defender activity, reboot, provider counts, completion, and history recovery. Repeated loss of required history after every patch cycle remains a real sizing defect.

5. **AutoBackup rollover operating as designed** — A channel in AutoBackup mode can approach maximum and create an archive without losing new writes. The primary rule intentionally does not page solely on its percentage. Separately verify archive creation, disk free space, ACL, archive discovery/forwarding, retention, and 1105 where applicable; archive accumulation can still exhaust disk.

6. **Event Forwarding collector concentration** — A WEC `ForwardedEvents` channel aggregates many endpoints and can churn rapidly or archive often. Compare subscription population, source rate, collector forwarding checkpoint, delivery mode, read-existing policy, archive handling, disk, and downstream lag. Size the collector channel and Splunk path together; a host exception can hide evidence loss across the fleet.

7. **Channel clear, reset, or configuration migration** — Approved clearing, EVTX relocation, LogMode change, max-size change, or OS upgrade can temporarily make oldest-history age short even with low future churn. Correlate Security 1102/System 104 where applicable, operator/change, before/after configuration, archived evidence, and policy effective time. Rebaseline only after preserving required records.

8. **Collector cannot read Security or an analytic channel** — Least-privilege, channel ACL, disabled provider, remote-call limitation, or localized/access error may yield null FileSize/history. Such rows must fail source health and never become low utilization. Test the exact service identity locally and grant only documented read rights needed for governed channels.

9. **Maximum-size policy intentionally below history objective during a migration** — A staged GPO or forwarder rollout may temporarily retain less history because a central platform is supposed to hold the authoritative copy. Prove end-to-end event continuity, checkpoint/backlog behavior, central retention, rollback, owner, and expiry. Local shortfall remains visible until formal policy changes.

**Safe suppression:** use lookup windows_eventlog_capacity_exceptions.csv after base detection. Require exact `host,log_name,policy_id`, inclusive numeric `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, reason, and accepted residual history. Reject wildcards, broad channel groups, open-ended dates, and exceptions for missing, inaccessible, duplicate, stale, or malformed telemetry. Suppression affects notification only. Recovery requires three complete consecutive samples with Retain not full and at/below threshold, or Circular either at/below threshold or meeting/exceeding required history.

detailedImplementation:
## Establish a mode-aware retention policy

Assign Windows Event Log, security/audit, application, Splunk collection, storage, source-health, and incident owners. Inventory the finite channels that matter on each role: commonly Security, System, Application, Setup, Windows PowerShell/PowerShell Operational, Defender, Sysmon, Task Scheduler, Failover Clustering, and workload-specific channels. Record exact channel name, role applicability, owner, enabled expectation, LogMode, maximum bytes, minimum local history hours, central-forwarding objective, archive policy, policy ID, and effective/retire epochs.

Run the collector locally with a service identity that can read configuration and oldest/newest records for every governed channel. Security and restricted analytic channels can require additional rights or channel ACLs; test the exact identity and grant only necessary read access. The identity needs no `SaveChanges`, log-clear, registry/GPO, audit-policy, archive-delete, or service-control permission. Splunk search users need read access to the local `windows` index and content app.

Understand Windows behavior before choosing thresholds. `MaximumSizeInBytes` is configured capacity; `FileSize` is current EVTX file bytes; `LogMode` determines what occurs at maximum. Circular replaces oldest records with new ones. AutoBackup archives the full file and starts another. Retain preserves existing events and discards incoming events until manually cleared. Microsoft's lower-level `EvtLogFull` property is always false for Circular and AutoBackup; it is meaningful for a sequential/Retain channel that cannot accept another event.

Therefore, “file >90%” alone is not an overflow alert for Circular. Once a circular file reaches its steady maximum it can remain near 100% forever while functioning exactly as configured. The relevant question is whether its oldest available event meets the required local-history objective. For Retain, near-full capacity is urgent because the channel can stop recording. AutoBackup requires archive creation and disk/retention health, not a current-file percentage page.

The catalogue examples use >90%, three five-minute samples, and per-channel required history such as 24 hours for high-rate operational logs or 72 hours for low-rate critical logs. These are local examples. Size from measured bytes/hour, event-size distribution, bursts, maintenance/forwarding outage tolerance, incident response horizon, disk, and archive/central retention. Exactly 90% is not a trigger; exactly the required history is acceptable.

## Collect one atomic governed-channel snapshot

For each inventory entry, call `Get-WinEvent -ListLog <exact-name>`. Capture `LogName`, `IsEnabled`, `LogFilePath`, `MaximumSizeInBytes`, `FileSize`, `LogMode`, `IsLogFull`, and `RecordCount`. On a nonempty channel, query one oldest and one newest event and convert `TimeCreated` to UTC epoch. Use bounded execution time and preserve errors by channel. Do not enumerate all events to find the endpoints.

Create one five-minute-aligned `sample_epoch`, actual `snapshot_epoch`, and UUID `snapshot_id` for the host. Emit one normalized row per expected channel, including policy. Counts and byte values must be nonnegative integers; maximum must be at least the Windows minimum 1,048,576 bytes; LogMode must be circular/autobackup/retain after case normalization. For an empty channel, set record count zero and `history_ready=0`; do not invent oldest/newest times. For a nonempty channel both times must be valid and ordered.

Emit one manifest only after every expected channel is queried and validated exactly once. `expected_channel_count` must match rows and distinct channel names. If any call is denied, channel absent, timeout occurs, history query fails, policy is malformed, or output truncates, set no complete manifest and write a separately classified health record. A partial host snapshot must not enter capacity decisions.

The script example is a skeleton. Production code must handle empty logs (where oldest/newest calls can throw), channels that become empty between calls, concurrent writes, access errors, canonical host identity, line-safe JSON, execution lock, policy activation, and manifest buffering. Preserve collector and policy versions.

## Configure the Windows PowerShell input and JSON parsing

Package code in `TA_windows_eventlog_capacity`. A representative stanza is:

```ini
[powershell://windows_eventlog_capacity]
script = . "$SplunkHome\etc\apps\TA_windows_eventlog_capacity\bin\collect-eventlog-capacity.ps1"
schedule = */5 * * * *
source = windows_eventlog_capacity
sourcetype = ms:windows:eventlog:capacity
index = windows
disabled = 0
```

Splunk's PowerShell handler indexes script output and supports schedules. Validate exact syntax on the qualified release. For Splunk Cloud, the script runs on the Windows Universal Forwarder and forwards data; it cannot query customer channels from managed search infrastructure. Use app `local` configuration and never edit vendor `default`.

Configure one JSON object per event with appropriate line breaking, no line merge, measured truncation, and JSON key extraction. Align `_time` with `snapshot_epoch` or keep it within 120 seconds. Verify effective settings using `btool inputs` and `btool props` with debug paths. Check script signature/path, Local System or approved service identity, index creation, forwarding queues, parsing tier, host metadata, duplicate deployment, and search ACL.

If optional 1104/1105/1108 collection is used, collect Security as XML through the Windows add-on and preserve provider `Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog`, channel, event ID, Computer, EventRecordID, and payload. Event 1104 specifically reports the Security log full under manual-clear/Retain behavior. Event 1105 reports AutoBackup rollover. Event 1108 reports a processing error for an incoming security event. These are corroborating impact/configuration events, not substitutes for all-channel inventory.

## Build source health before capacity alerting

Maintain an expected-host/channel table and compare it with each manifest. Report missing host or channel, unknown channel, disabled governed channel, duplicate row, two snapshot IDs for one slot, no/multiple/incomplete manifest, count mismatch, stale/future/misaligned time, collector overrun, null/negative/fractional byte or record values, max below Windows minimum, percentage outside a reasonable allocation tolerance, invalid mode, Retain-full inconsistency, inaccessible history, oldest after newest, newest in the future, and policy drift.

For Circular history, low event volume can make oldest age long even with tiny files; that is correctly healthy for a history objective but may still fail an event-source freshness objective. Conversely, a channel can meet byte capacity yet have no new events because its provider failed. Maintain provider/event freshness independently.

For AutoBackup, inventory archive path/pattern, successful archive creation, disk free space, archive count/age, ACL, backup/forwarding, and retention. A new current file at 1% is not proof that the previous archive is safe. Event 1105 covers Security rollover but archive handling needs broader checks.

The primary rule allows up to ten minutes for collection/indexing and looks for the newest expected slot at `floor((now()-120)/300)*300`. Measure p99 query runtime and index delay. If oldest-event queries exceed the window, reduce the governed list, fix channel/host performance, stagger fleets, or revise schedule and tests—do not accept partial manifests.

## Create and interpret the SPL

Save the sidecar query as `windows_eventlog_capacity_retention_risk`; run every five minutes approximately two minutes after the slot; trigger when result count exceeds zero. The 30-minute base horizon provides enough rows for persistence and delay.

Numeric conversion occurs before validation. Epochs must be aligned integer slots and collected within two minutes. `utilization_pct` is bytes divided by maximum bytes times 100, not record count or free disk. A tolerance up to 110% accommodates allocation/observation behavior but values beyond it are rejected for investigation.

History validity accepts an explicit empty channel only with zero records and `history_ready=0`; nonempty channels require ordered oldest/newest times. Manifest reconciliation then requires one manifest and equality among expected, actual, valid, and distinct channel rows. Snapshot cardinality rejects competing IDs per host/slot.

Risk semantics are mode-specific:
- Retain + `is_log_full=1` yields `retain_full`, regardless of percentage rounding.
- Retain + percentage strictly above policy yields `retain_capacity`.
- Circular yields `circular_retention_shortfall` only when percentage is above policy and retained history is below objective.
- AutoBackup never qualifies on these fields alone.

After deterministic ordering, a three-row rolling window requires all three samples risky, exactly ten minutes between first and last starts, and unchanged threshold/history policy. The latest expected slot prevents old incidents from reappearing after missing current data. Results preserve peak percentage and minimum retained history.

Incident identity is host/channel/mode/policy. Throttle a page for one evaluation period while retaining results. A mode change creates a new policy context and must be reviewed. Recovery needs three complete samples under the rule described in `knownFalsePositives`; no data or inaccessible oldest record cannot recover.

## Validate bytes, history, modes, and Windows UI

Run every `controlTest` variant in an isolated index with fixed dispatch. Assert strict percentage and history boundaries, full-at-low-percentage behavior, AutoBackup exclusion, explicit empty semantics, complete cardinality, cadence, latest slot, and policy stability. Test 1,048,576-byte minimum, large 64-bit sizes, file/max rounding, rapidly changing record count, channel becoming empty between calls, inaccessible Security, Unicode/slash channel names, host rename, clock skew, and two collectors.

On Windows canaries, compare a snapshot at the same time with:

```powershell
Get-WinEvent -ListLog Security | Format-List *
Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Oldest -MaxEvents 1
Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -MaxEvents 1
wevtutil gl Security /f:xml
```

In **Event Viewer**, right-click the channel and open **Properties**. Compare log path, current observed file, maximum size, overwrite/archive/manual policy, oldest/newest records, and record count. Accept bounded differences caused by concurrent writes and record exact command times. Verify Circular, AutoBackup, and Retain in a disposable lab. Do not fill or clear a production Security log to test.

Use synthetic fixtures for 1104/1105 correlation unless an isolated lab safely exercises those modes. Confirm 1104 only as Security-full evidence and 1105 as archive rollover. Test 1108 separately as processing failure, not utilization. Record Windows/PowerShell/forwarder/add-on/Splunk versions, policy and fixture revisions, search job ID, expected/actual output, runtime, and operator.

Measure collector CPU/time, oldest-event call latency, JSON bytes, event rate, indexing lag, search duration, dashboard cardinality, and AutoBackup archive growth at fleet scale. Keep draft status until Windows Event Log, security/audit, application, storage, and Splunk owners approve.

## Operationalize capacity and retention response

Alert title: `Windows event channel capacity/retention risk for 15m: <host>/<log>`. Include mode/full flag, current/max bytes and percentage, record count, oldest/newest UTC, retained/required hours, peak/minimum across three samples, source health, policy owner, active changes, exception, disk/archive status, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify complete snapshots, exact channel/mode/policy, native configuration, current file, and oldest/newest records.
2. Determine whether risk is stopped writes (Retain) or shortened history (Circular); inspect 1104/1105/1108 where applicable.
3. Calculate measured bytes/events per hour and identify top providers/EventIDs, recent audit/provider/configuration changes, bursts, and forwarding backlog.
4. Verify Splunk/WEF checkpoint and central retention continuity independently; local history and central evidence are different controls.
5. For AutoBackup, verify archive file, disk free, archive retention/protection, and ingestion/backup.
6. Choose a reviewed remediation: increase maximum size within disk budget, reduce unjustified noisy logging, correct forwarding latency, move/archive safely, or revise an explicitly approved history objective.
7. Validate Event Viewer/native configuration, event continuity, and three healthy recovery samples.

Never automatically clear a channel, delete/archive EVTX, call `SaveChanges`, run `wevtutil sl/cl`, change retention/AutoBackup/max size, disable audit/provider logging, stop EventLog, reboot, or alter forwarding. Clearing destroys local evidence; changing Retain can overwrite evidence; oversized logs can consume disk; audit changes can violate policy.

Apply lookup windows_eventlog_capacity_exceptions.csv only after result generation. Preserve exact bounded scope and residual-risk approval. Review the channel inventory, bytes/history policies, collector rights, exceptions, archive handling, source-health logic, and dashboard quarterly and after GPO, audit, provider, role, WEF, Windows, forwarder, add-on, or Splunk changes.

## Troubleshoot without turning unknown into green

- **`Get-WinEvent -ListLog` denied:** run under the collection identity and inspect channel ACL/Security-log rights. Grant narrow read capability, not blanket administration.
- **FileSize null while events exist:** inspect actual object properties and PowerShell/.NET version, local versus remote behavior, and LogFilePath access. Fail health; do not use zero.
- **`wevtutil gl` has maxSize but no FileSize:** expected; use EventLogConfiguration/FileSize for current bytes.
- **Circular channel always near 100%:** normal steady-state behavior. Evaluate oldest history against objective instead of paging on percentage alone.
- **Retain says full but percentage is lower:** trust the native full flag and inspect file allocation/configuration timing; result correctly remains risky.
- **Oldest query throws on empty log:** emit record_count zero/history not ready only after confirming emptiness; other errors remain incomplete.
- **Oldest history becomes short after clear:** correlate clear/configuration events and preserved archive/change authorization; do not call it capacity growth without rate evidence.
- **AutoBackup current file drops suddenly:** inspect archive creation and disk. Rollover is expected; archive loss is not.
- **Snapshot and Event Viewer differ:** align host/channel/time, refresh UI, compare bytes versus displayed KB, and account for concurrent writes.
- **No alert but Splunk events are missing:** this rule monitors local channel capacity/history, not forwarding completeness. Use checkpoint/source-continuity monitoring.
- **CIM search returns unrelated changes:** expected; there is no declared CIM equivalent for atomic channel capacity and retained history.
grandmaExplanation: We check whether important Windows logs still hold enough history and whether a log configured never to overwrite is close to stopping. We account for how each log behaves when full, so a normally full circular log does not create a useless alarm.
